chunks: ʿAlī narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment concerning a mukātab who was killed. He said: “Whatever portion of him had been freed is calculated, and for that the blood money of a free person is to be paid; and whatever portion of him remained enslaved, the blood money of a slave applies for that.”

key_terms.دِيَةُ الْحُرِّ: the blood money due for a free person
key_terms.دِيَةُ الْعَبْدِ: the blood money due for a slave
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: a slave under a manumission contract who is earning or paying for freedom

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the diyah of a mukātab if he is killed?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding a mukātab who is killed. The compensation is divided proportionally: the freed portion is assessed as the diyah of a free person, and the remaining enslaved portion is assessed as the diyah of a slave.
